simple.meaning: רָעֵב (râʻêb) is a Hebrew concept word meaning “to hunger.” BibleIQ follows how Scripture develops this idea across its occurrences.
simple.biblicalBackground: The concept appears 13 times across Genesis, Deuteronomy, Psalms, Proverbs, Isaiah, and 1 more, beginning at Genesis 41:55. Its contexts include family, righteousness, land, Egypt.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to רָעֵב (H7456).
simple.whyItMatters: Concept words shape biblical themes. BibleIQ keeps the concept grounded in actual verse evidence instead of starting with a later theological definition.

definitions.usage: (suffer to) famish, (be, have, suffer, suffer to) hunger(-ry).
definitions.full: H7456. raeb רָעֵב verb be hungry (Late Hebrew id. Hiph`il and derivatives; Assyrian rûbatu, hunger; Arabic be roomy, voracious , desire vehemently ; Ethiopic be hungry ); — Qal Perfect 3masculine singular ׳ר Isa 9:19 ; 44:12 ; 3 plural רָעֵ֑בוּ Psa 34:11 ; Imperfect 3masculine singular יִרְעַב Isa 8:21 , 1 plural נִרְעַב Jer 42:14 , etc.; — be hungry Isa 8:21 ; Gen 41:55 (E; of land, = have famine), Jer 42:14 ( לַלֶּחֶם ), Isa 49:10 (|| צמא ), 65:13 (|| id. ; opposed to אכל ), Psa 50:12 if I should be hungry (of ׳י ), Prov 6:30 ; 19:15 . Hiph`il allow one to hunger , subject ׳י : Imperfect 3masculine singular וַיַּרְעִבֶ֑ךָ Deut 8:3 (opposed to וַיַּאֲִכלְךָ ), נֶפֶשׁ יַרְעִיב Prov 10:3 .

occurrences.englishText: When all the land of Egypt was famished, the people cried to Pharaoh for bread, and Pharaoh said to all the Egyptians, “Go to Joseph. What he says to you, do.”

He humbled you, allowed you to be hungry, and fed you with manna, which you didn’t know, neither did your fathers know, that he might teach you that man does not live by bread only, but man lives by every word that proceeds out of Yahweh’s mouth.
Come, you children, listen to me.
If I were hungry, I would not tell you,
Yahweh will not allow the soul of the righteous to go hungry,
Slothfulness casts into a deep sleep.
They will pass through it, very distressed and hungry. It will happen that when they are hungry, they will worry, and curse by their king and by their God. They will turn their faces upward,
Through Yahweh of Armies’ wrath, the land is burned up;
They shall not hunger nor thirst;
saying, “No; but we will go into the land of Egypt, where we will see no war, nor hear the sound of the trumpet, nor have hunger of bread; and there will we dwell:” ’
